Thank you for considering a career with the Research Foundation of The City University of New York (RFCUNY).

 
The team at RFCUNY is made up of dedicated, talented professionals committed to providing the services that allow CUNY researchers, faculty, and staff to focus on their intellectual curiosity and scientific discoveries.

 
We are pleased that you are interested in exploring opportunities to join RFCUNY.

 

 
Primary Location:
The CITY COLLEGE of NEW YORK 
 

 
Bargaining Unit:

 
No

 

 
The City University of New York's (CUNY) Building Performance Laboratory (CUNY BPL), in partnership with the City of New York, is seeking qualified energy management professionals to join the Department of Citywide Administrative Services (DCAS) Division of Energy Management (DEM). DEM serves as the central hub for energy management across City government operations. It is responsible for developing the City’s annual Heat, Light, and Power Budget; managing the City's electricity, natural gas, and steam accounts; assisting agency partners in identifying and pursuing energy-saving opportunities; overseeing energy efficiency and clean power generation projects across the City’s portfolio; and implementing best practices in operations and maintenance. DEM is specifically tasked with leading the City's efforts to reduce emissions from City government operations by 40% by 2025 and 50% by 2030 from the baseline.

 

 
CUNY BPL seeks to hire an Associate Data Analyst to support property and energy data management for the DEM’s Data Analytics & Reporting Team (DART). The Associate Data Analyst will support data collection from City agencies and other sources while maintaining property data in a Salesforce environment and energy data in a SQL database. This role also supports the compliance process required by Local Law 84 of 2009.

 

 
This is a hybrid position working on-site 3 days a week at 1 Centre St, New York, NY 10007. NYC residency may be required for continued employment. Immigration sponsorship is not available.

 

 
Responsibilities:

 
Under this assignment, the person’s responsibilities may include the following:

 

 
  
Support the annual Local Law 84 building energy benchmarking process for City buildings.

  
Collect and clean property data to ensure accuracy and integrity.

  
Identify and resolve data discrepancies proactively.

  
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to understand data needs and respond to internal and external stakeholders.

  
Analyze problems, propose potential solutions, and implement the most effective solution.

  
Structure large property and energy data sets to extract usable information.

  
Work with agency and external teams to support data analysis, reporting, and measurement for all agency-led initiatives.

  
Prepare property- or energy-related data and input into Salesforce or SQL data front-end, in response to agency communications via emails or extracted from external sources.

  
Work on formalizing various data maintenance policies.

  
Collect and analyze datasets to generate actionable insights.

  
Demonstrate the ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.

  
Collaborate with various departments using strong interpersonal skills.
Undertake additional responsibilities as needed.
 
 

 
Qualifications:

 
The ideal candidate will bring the following skills and experience to this position:

 
  
A bachelor’s degree is required.

  
A minimum of 1 year data management experience is preferred.

  
Strong, verifiable experience in data analysis, data visualization, and reporting.

  
Flexibility to handle multiple responsibilities and deadlines simultaneously.

  
Self-motivated and able to work independently as well as part of a team.

  
Strong, verifiable understanding of data management best practices.

  
Strong analytical skills with ability to collect, organize, analyze, and disseminate significant amounts of information with attention to detail and accuracy.

  
Thoughtful and curious with a data-driven approach to solving business problems.

  
Commitment to delivering measurable results and a proven ability to manage projects to successful completion.

  
Advanced knowledge of Microsoft 365 stack including MS Excel and MS PowerPoint.

  
Basic knowledge of Python, R, or SQL are a plus.

  
Familiarity with issues pertaining to energy efficiency in existing buildings.

 
 

 
Pay Range:

 
Minimum - Maximum: $70,000 per year

ROLE OVERVIEW

Job description

Gain America's Early Careers program places new and recent graduates into entry-level Junior Data Analyst roles with leading employers across the New York, NY area. Turn data into insight for enterprise teams while building analytics skills that scale. This is a launchpad: you'll gain real production experience with mentorship and structured onboarding.

We welcome new graduates and students, including candidates on OPT, CPT, or STEM-OPT work authorization.

Work model: Hybrid / on-site · New York, NY
You'll work with: SQL, Python, Excel, Power BI or Tableau, data visualization

What you'll do

Write SQL queries and prepare datasets for analysis
Build dashboards and reports in Power BI or Tableau
Support data-quality checks and ad-hoc analysis
Present findings clearly to stakeholders

What you bring

A degree in a quantitative or related field
Working SQL and spreadsheet skills; some Python a plus
An analytical, detail-oriented mindset
Clear written and verbal communication

Gain America is a technology staffing partner that helps early-career talent launch with leading employers. You'll work with a dedicated recruiter who supports you from first conversation through offer.

Apply to join the Gain America Early Careers talent network in the New York, NY area.
